exam: Sweep 2 - Programming for the Web (SEN Online)

parts.prompt: Select all that apply: Which benefits are provided by Progressive Web Apps (PWAs)?

explanation.correct: PWAs are websites that act like apps. They can send push notifications, load fast (thanks to caching) and work offline.

options.A: Right. PWAs can send push notifications.
options.B: Right. Cached files make them load fast.
options.C: Right. Service workers let them work offline.

explanation.strategy: 'Select all' means judging each option on its own. Sometimes all are right.

parts.prompt: A small business wants to build a platform where customers can browse products and receive order notifications. However, they cannot afford a native mobile app. Which solution should they choose?

explanation.correct: A PWA is cheaper than a native app but can still send notifications. That meets both needs.

options.A: Right. App-like features, including notifications, at website cost.
options.B: Wrong. A static site can't send order notifications.
options.C: Wrong. A normal Flask website can't send push notifications to the device.
options.D: Wrong. They can't afford a native mobile app.

explanation.strategy: Match every detail in the scenario: low cost AND notifications. Only one option meets both.

parts.prompt: Select all components of a data packet: (Select all that apply.)

explanation.correct: A packet has a header (addresses and info), a payload (the actual data) and a trailer (error checking).

options.A: Right. The header holds source, destination and order.
options.B: Right. The payload is the data being sent.
options.C: Right. The trailer marks the end and checks for errors.

explanation.strategy: 'Select all' means judging each option. Remember the three parts: start, middle, end.

parts.prompt: Which type of DNS query expects the DNS server to return the correct IP address or an error message?

explanation.correct: In a recursive query, the DNS server must do all the work and return the IP address or an error.

options.A: Wrong. In an iterative query the server may just point you to another server.
options.B: Wrong. 'Direct query' is not a DNS query type.
options.C: Wrong. A non-recursive query is answered only from what the server already knows.
options.D: Right. The server returns the full answer or an error.

explanation.strategy: Match the detail 'answer or an error' to the definition. Cross out made-up terms like 'Direct Query'.

parts.prompt: Which protocol is responsible for translating domain names like www.example.com Links to an external site. into IP addresses?

explanation.correct: DNS (Domain Name System) turns names like example.com into IP addresses.

options.A: Wrong. HTTP transfers web pages.
options.B: Wrong. SMTP sends email.
options.C: Wrong. FTP transfers files.
options.D: Right. DNS is the internet's phone book.

explanation.strategy: Spot the keyword: 'domain names' matches Domain Name System.

parts.prompt: Which of the following protocols is responsible for retrieving emails from a mail server to a local device?

explanation.correct: POP3 downloads emails from the server to your device.

options.A: Right. POP3 downloads mail to the local device.
options.B: Marked wrong by the key. But IMAP also retrieves email. It keeps it synced on the server too.
options.C: Wrong. DNS finds IP addresses.
options.D: Wrong. SMTP sends email. It doesn't retrieve it.

explanation.strategy: Separate send (SMTP) from receive (POP3, IMAP). If two options fit, pick the one closest to the exact words: 'to a local device' = POP3.
explanation.key_note: IMAP (B) also retrieves email from a mail server. POP3 is the better match for 'to a local device' because it downloads and usually removes mail from the server. But IMAP is not wrong.

parts.prompt: A software developer needs to ensure that their distributed software is secure and untampered. What process should they use to verify the software’s authenticity?

explanation.correct: A digital signature proves who made the software and that it hasn't been changed.

options.A: Wrong. A symmetric key hides data. It doesn't prove who sent it.
options.B: Wrong. AES encryption keeps data secret but doesn't prove the author.
options.C: Right. Signatures give authenticity and integrity.
options.D: Wrong. A hash checks for changes but not who made it. MD5 is also weak now.

explanation.strategy: Match the keyword: 'authenticity' (who made it) = digital signature.

parts.prompt: Which encryption algorithm is known for using the same key for both encryption and decryption?

explanation.correct: AES is symmetric encryption: the same key locks and unlocks the data.

options.A: Wrong. RSA is asymmetric: it uses a public and private key pair.
options.B: Wrong. SHA-256 is a hash, not encryption. It can't be decrypted.
options.C: Wrong. 'EEC' is likely ECC (elliptic curve). That is asymmetric.
options.D: Right. AES uses one shared key.

explanation.strategy: Sort the options into groups: symmetric, asymmetric, hashing. Then pick from the right group.

parts.prompt: Which of the following are common data mining techniques? (Select all that apply)

explanation.correct: Data mining finds patterns. Clustering, regression and classification are mining techniques.

options.A: Right. Clustering groups similar data.
options.B: Right. Regression predicts number values.
options.C: Wrong. Normalisation cleans or scales data before mining. It is not mining itself.
options.D: Right. Classification sorts data into labelled groups.

explanation.strategy: 'Select all' means judging each option. Ask: does it find patterns, or just prepare the data?

parts.prompt: Which data mining technique is used to discover relationships between variables, such as identifying products frequently bought together?

explanation.correct: Association finds items that often go together, like 'people who buy bread also buy butter'.

options.A: Wrong. Classification sorts data into known groups.
options.B: Wrong. Regression predicts a number.
options.C: Right. Association finds relationships like 'bought together'.
options.D: Wrong. Clustering groups similar items but doesn't find 'bought together' rules.

explanation.strategy: Match the example: 'frequently bought together' = association.

parts.prompt: What is the purpose of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) developed by the W3C?

options.text: To standardise the access of web pages and web content
To provide a framework for making web content more accessible
To define security protocols for web applications

explanation.correct: WCAG gives a set of guidelines for making web content accessible to people with disabilities.

options.A: Wrong. Close, but WCAG is about accessibility, not 'access' in general.
options.B: Right. It's a framework for accessible web content.
options.C: Wrong. That describes RDF / the semantic web.
options.D: Wrong. WCAG is not about security.

explanation.strategy: Use the name: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines. The answer should say 'accessible'.

parts.prompt: Which W3C standard is specifically designed to help developers create accessible rich internet applications?

explanation.correct: WAI-ARIA adds labels and roles to dynamic page parts so screen readers can understand them.

options.A: Wrong. RDF describes data for machines.
options.B: Wrong. CSP (Content Security Policy) is a security standard.
options.C: Right. ARIA = Accessible Rich Internet Applications.
options.D: Wrong. WCAG is general guidelines, not built for rich apps.

explanation.strategy: Expand the acronym. ARIA spells out the exact words in the question.

parts.prompt: What type of database uses tables to store data and is based on Structured Query Language (SQL)?

explanation.correct: A relational database stores data in linked tables and uses SQL.

options.A: Right. Tables plus SQL = relational.
options.B: Wrong. NoSQL databases often don't use tables or SQL.
options.C: Wrong. A flat file is one simple table with no SQL.
options.D: Wrong. 'SQL database' is an informal name, not the correct type name.

explanation.strategy: Pick the proper technical term over an informal nickname.

parts.prompt: In a web development system, what is the primary role of the server-side (back-end)?

options.text: Managing data storage and application logic

explanation.correct: The back-end runs on the server. It stores data and runs the app's logic.

options.A: Wrong. CSS styling is front-end.
options.B: Wrong. Layout design is front-end.
options.C: Wrong. JavaScript interactivity in the browser is front-end.
options.D: Right. Data and logic happen on the server.

explanation.strategy: Three options are front-end jobs. The odd one out is the back-end answer.

parts.prompt: Why is it important for developers to test their web applications across different browsers?

options.text: To reduce the cost of development
To decrease the application's loading speed
To maintain consistent appearance and functionality
To ensure the application uses the latest browser features

explanation.correct: Browsers can show pages differently. Testing in each one keeps the look and function the same.

options.A: Wrong. Extra testing adds cost.
options.B: Wrong. You never want slower loading.
options.C: Right. Consistency across browsers is the goal.
options.D: Wrong. New features may not work in every browser.

explanation.strategy: Rule out options that are bad outcomes ('decrease loading speed' means slower).

parts.prompt: What is the primary purpose of the Console Panel in browser developer tools?

options.text: Inspect and modify HTML and CSS

explanation.correct: The Console panel lets you run JavaScript and see errors and log messages.

options.A: Wrong. That's the Network panel.
options.B: Wrong. That's the Application (or Storage) panel.
options.C: Right. The Console runs and debugs JavaScript.
options.D: Wrong. That's the Elements panel.

explanation.strategy: Each option is a different DevTools panel. Match the panel name to its job.

parts.prompt: Which feature of CSS allows developers to define values like colours and spacing to ensure consistency across a web application?

explanation.correct: CSS variables store values like colours once, then reuse them everywhere for consistency.

options.A: Wrong. Media queries change styles for screen sizes.
options.B: Wrong. Preprocessors (like Sass) have variables too, but they are not a built-in CSS feature.
options.C: Right. e.g. --main-colour: blue; used across the site.
options.D: Wrong. Flexbox is for layout.

explanation.strategy: Spot the keyword: 'define values' matches variables.

parts.prompt: Which CSS methodology helps in writing scalable and maintainable CSS by following a component-based approach?

explanation.correct: BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) is a naming method that splits CSS into reusable components.

options.A: Right. BEM is a component-based CSS method.
options.B: Wrong. Grid is a layout tool, not a methodology.
options.C: Wrong. Semantic HTML is about meaningful tags, not CSS.
options.D: Wrong. Inline styling is hard to maintain.

explanation.strategy: The question says 'methodology'. Only one option is a way of organising CSS.

parts.prompt: Which Git feature allows developers to work on new features without affecting the main codebase?

explanation.correct: A branch is a separate copy of the code where you can build a feature safely.

options.A: Wrong. Merge joins a branch back into main.
options.B: Wrong. Push uploads commits to a remote.
options.C: Wrong. Commit saves a snapshot of changes.
options.D: Right. Branches keep new work apart from main.

explanation.strategy: Match the detail: 'without affecting main' = working apart = branch.

parts.prompt: What is the primary purpose of version control in web application development?

options.text: To track and manage changes to code

explanation.correct: Version control tracks every change to code, so you can see history and undo mistakes.

options.A: Wrong. Graphics are made with design tools.
options.B: Right. Tracking and managing code changes.
options.C: Wrong. UI design is a different job.
options.D: Wrong. Not about performance.

explanation.strategy: Use the name: 'version' control = managing versions (changes).

parts.prompt: Why is it beneficial for developers to use a code library instead of writing custom code from scratch?

options.text: It allows for greater creativity in coding
It increases the complexity of the project
It speeds up development and reduces errors
It limits the options for customisation

explanation.correct: Libraries hold tested code you can reuse. This saves time and cuts bugs.

options.A: Wrong. Libraries don't mainly add creativity.
options.B: Wrong. That's a downside, not a benefit.
options.C: Right. Faster development, fewer errors.
options.D: Wrong. That's a downside, not a benefit.

explanation.strategy: The question asks 'why is it beneficial'. Cross out the negatives.

parts.prompt: Which of the following best describes a common use case for code libraries in front-end development?

options.text: Creating user interfaces and managing state

explanation.correct: Front-end libraries like React help build user interfaces and manage state (the data the page shows).

options.A: Wrong. Encrypting user data is mainly a back-end job.
options.B: Right. UI and state are front-end tasks.
options.C: Wrong. Database setup is back-end.
options.D: Wrong. Server code is back-end.

explanation.strategy: The question says 'front-end'. Rule out every back-end task.

parts.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of using open-source software in web development?

explanation.correct: Open source code is free and anyone can change it. 'Proprietary control' means one owner controls it, which is the opposite.

options.A: Right answer (NOT a benefit). Proprietary means closed and owned.
options.B: Wrong choice. Free access is a benefit.
options.C: Wrong choice. Community development is a benefit.
options.D: Wrong choice. Being able to modify code is a benefit.

explanation.strategy: In a NOT question, look for the word that clashes with the topic. 'Proprietary' is the opposite of open source.

parts.prompt: Which open-source version control system is widely used in web development to track changes in code?

explanation.correct: Git is the most widely used version control system in web development.

options.A: Right. Git (used with GitHub) is the standard.
options.B: Wrong. CVS is open source but old and rarely used now.
options.C: Wrong. Mercurial is open source but much less common.
options.D: Wrong. Subversion is open source but less common now.

explanation.strategy: All options are open source. The deciding word is 'widely used'.

parts.prompt: What does the term "minification" refer to in the context of web development?

options.text: Increasing file sizes to improve performance
Compressing images for faster load times

explanation.correct: Minification removes spaces, line breaks and comments from code. The file gets smaller and loads faster.

options.A: Right. It strips characters the computer doesn't need.
options.B: Wrong. Comments are removed, not added.
options.C: Wrong. Bigger files load slower.
options.D: Wrong. That's image compression, not minification.

explanation.strategy: Use the word: 'mini' = make smaller. Rule out anything that adds.

parts.prompt: Which of the following factors can significantly impact web page load times?

explanation.correct: Large images are often the biggest files on a page. Their size and format strongly affect load time.

options.A: Wrong. Font style has little effect (unless loading many web fonts).
options.B: Wrong. Colours don't change load time.
options.C: Right. Big, uncompressed images slow pages a lot.
options.D: Wrong. Rare on modern sites, and not the common cause.

explanation.strategy: Look for the word 'significantly'. Pick the option with the biggest effect.

parts.prompt: Which key feature of a CMS allows content creators to collaborate effectively by defining roles and permissions?

explanation.correct: User management lets a CMS set roles (like editor or admin) and permissions for each person.

options.A: Wrong. Plugins add extra features.
options.B: Right. Roles and permissions are user management.
options.C: Wrong. Content organisation sorts pages and posts.
options.D: Wrong. Themes change how the site looks.

explanation.strategy: Spot the keyword: 'roles and permissions' are about users.

parts.prompt: Which feature of a CMS is most directly related to defining the visual appearance of a website?

explanation.correct: Themes and templates control how a CMS site looks.

options.A: Wrong. Content organisation is about structure, not looks.
options.B: Right. Themes set the visual style.
options.C: Wrong. Plugins add features.
options.D: Wrong. User management controls who can do what.

explanation.strategy: Spot the keyword: 'visual appearance' = theme.

parts.prompt: Which of the following are components of back-end development? (Select all that apply)

explanation.correct: The back-end includes the server, database, APIs and security. All four are part of it.

options.A: Right. Security like login checks runs on the back-end.
options.B: Right. APIs connect the front-end to the back-end.
options.C: Right. The server runs the back-end code.
options.D: Right. The database stores the data.

explanation.strategy: 'Select all' means judging each option. Ask: does this run on the server side?

parts.prompt: Select all security responsibilities of back-end development: (Select all that apply.)

explanation.correct: The back-end must protect data, secure its APIs and check who users are.

options.A: Right. Sensitive data must be encrypted.
options.B: Right. APIs need protection from misuse.
options.C: Right. Login checks must happen on the server.

explanation.strategy: 'Select all' means judging each option. All three are server-side security jobs.

parts.prompt: A developer needs to fetch a user’s data using an ORM. Which of the following represents the correct approach?

explanation.correct: An ORM lets you use objects and methods in code instead of writing SQL. 'User.objects.get(id=1)' does this.

options.A: Wrong. Not a real ORM method. It's just a made-up command.
options.B: Right. Uses a class (User) and a method. This is Django ORM style.
options.C: Wrong. This is raw SQL, not ORM.
options.D: Wrong. This is a MongoDB (NoSQL) query, not a relational ORM.

explanation.strategy: Look for the option that uses a class and a method. ORM = objects, not SQL text. (In Flask-SQLAlchemy it would look like db.session.get(User, 1).)

parts.prompt: Which of the following is a typical responsibility of a web framework in handling a web request?

options.text: Serving static content such as images or CSS.
Storing data permanently in the database.

explanation.correct: A web framework (like Flask) decides which function handles each URL (routing) and processes the request.

options.A: Wrong. Static files are often served by the web server, not the framework's main job.
options.B: Wrong. Connection pools are handled by the database driver or ORM.
options.C: Right. Routing and request handling is the framework's core job.
options.D: Wrong. The database stores data, not the framework.

explanation.strategy: Pick the most typical job, not one it can sometimes do. Think of Flask's @app.route.

parts.prompt: Which of the following tasks can be automated with a shell script in web development?

options.text: Creating directories and backing up log files
Managing user session states in a browser

explanation.correct: Shell scripts automate file and system jobs, like making folders and backing up logs.

options.A: Wrong. Form validation runs in the browser with JavaScript or on the server.
options.B: Right. File and folder tasks suit shell scripts.
options.C: Wrong. Session state is handled by the web app.
options.D: Wrong. Layout is done with HTML and CSS.

explanation.strategy: Shell scripts run on the system, not in the browser. Rule out browser tasks.

parts.prompt: What is the purpose of the #!/bin/bash line at the start of a shell script?

options.text: It ensures the script is interpreted by Bash
It prevents the script from executing on the server
It comments out the first line of the script
It adds debugging information to the script

explanation.correct: The '#!/bin/bash' line (called a shebang) tells the system to run the script with Bash.

options.A: Right. It picks the interpreter.
options.B: Wrong. It helps the script run. It doesn't stop it.
options.C: Wrong. It starts with # but it is special, not just a comment.
options.D: Wrong. It adds no debugging info.

explanation.strategy: Notice the word 'bash' in the line itself. It points to the answer.

parts.prompt: What does the following SQL query do? SELECT department COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY department;

options.text: Returns the number of employees in each department
Counts all employees with the same salary
Groups employees by their last name
Selects the first name and last name of all employees

explanation.correct: GROUP BY department makes one group per department. COUNT(*) counts the rows in each group.

options.A: Right. Number of employees per department.
options.B: Wrong. Salary isn't in the query.
options.C: Wrong. Last name isn't in the query.
options.D: Wrong. Names aren't selected.

explanation.strategy: Rule out options that mention columns not in the query. (Real SQL needs a comma: SELECT department, COUNT(*).)

parts.prompt: Which of the following SQL commands is used to retrieve data from a database?

explanation.correct: SELECT reads (retrieves) data from a database.

options.A: Wrong. UPDATE changes existing data.
options.B: Right. SELECT gets data.
options.C: Wrong. DELETE removes data.
options.D: Wrong. INSERT adds new data.

explanation.strategy: Match each command to its job. Only one reads without changing anything.

parts.prompt: In which scenario would it be more appropriate to use SQL rather than ORM?

options.text: Rapid prototyping of a CRUD-heavy application
When the project is mainly focused on automated database interactions

explanation.correct: Raw SQL is better when you need special features of one database that the ORM can't do.

options.A: Right. ORMs hide database-specific features.
options.B: Wrong. Rapid CRUD prototyping is where ORM shines.
options.C: Wrong. ORM makes switching databases easier.
options.D: Wrong. ORM is good at routine database tasks.

explanation.strategy: Three options are ORM strengths. The odd one out is the SQL case.

parts.prompt: Which factor contributes to ORM’s lower performance compared to SQL?

options.text: Abstraction layer that generates SQL automatically
Lack of support for CRUD operations
ORM's inability to execute SQL queries

explanation.correct: The ORM adds an extra layer that turns your code into SQL. That extra step can make it slower.

options.A: Wrong. ORMs usually work with many databases.
options.B: Right. The abstraction layer adds overhead.
options.C: Wrong. ORMs fully support CRUD.
options.D: Wrong. ORMs do run SQL, they generate it.

explanation.strategy: Rule out options that are simply false facts. Only one gives a real cause of slowness.

parts.prompt: What is a key advantage of early collaboration between front-end and back-end teams during the development process?

options.text: It allows the back-end to be finished before the front-end begins.
It eliminates the need for API documentation.
It ensures faster UI design so that other parts of the project will advance.
It helps reduce integration issues between front-end and back-end.

explanation.correct: Talking early means both teams agree on how they connect (like the API). This stops problems when joining the parts.

options.A: Wrong. That's sequential work, not collaboration.
options.B: Wrong. API documentation is still needed.
options.C: Wrong. Speeding UI design isn't the main benefit.
options.D: Right. Fewer integration problems.

explanation.strategy: Watch for 'eliminates the need'. Collaboration rarely removes a step.

parts.prompt: How does shared responsibility between front-end and back-end teams improve overall performance?

options.text: Helps reduce unnecessary API calls and optimise server load times.
Ensures that the front-end team is accountable for performance issues.
Increases the number of API calls to the back-end.
Removes the need for performance monitoring tools.

explanation.correct: When both teams share responsibility, they plan together to cut extra API calls and speed up the server.

options.A: Right. Fewer calls and faster responses.
options.B: Wrong. Blaming one team is not shared responsibility.
options.C: Wrong. More API calls hurts performance.
options.D: Wrong. You still need monitoring.

explanation.strategy: Check each option against the key word 'shared'. Options that blame one side don't fit.

parts.prompt: Your team is designing a PWA for a video tutorial platform. Users complain that videos auto-play with sound, disrupting their experience. Which UI/UX principle should your team prioritise to address this issue?

explanation.correct: The key marks multimedia performance as the answer: handling video well, including not auto-playing sound.

options.A: Wrong. Fonts are not the problem.
options.B: Marked wrong by the key. But auto-playing sound does clash with screen readers, so this is arguable.
options.C: Wrong. Navigation feedback isn't the issue.
options.D: Right (per key). It's the only option about how media behaves.

explanation.strategy: Match the scenario's topic. The problem is about video, so pick the option about multimedia.
explanation.key_note: The real principle is user control of media (don't autoplay with sound). None of the options says this. D is the closest match to 'videos'. But B is also defensible: WCAG says autoplaying audio interferes with screen readers.

parts.prompt: Which feature of a PWA ensures that users can install the app directly from a website without going through an app store?

explanation.correct: A PWA can be installed straight from the browser to the home screen. This is called being installable.

options.A: Wrong. Responsive design fits different screen sizes.
options.B: Wrong. Service workers give offline use and caching.
options.C: Right. Installable = add to home screen without an app store.
options.D: Wrong. App shell is about fast loading of the basic layout.

explanation.strategy: Spot the keyword: 'install' matches 'installable'.
